newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels ready for peace talks on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels ready for peace talks on Thursday.

text.p: Zaire rebels said on Monday they were ready for talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko's representatives on Thursday to prepare for a meeting between him and rebel chief Laurent Kabila.

Mwanze Kongolo, justice commissioner in the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo-Zaire (AFDL), told Reuters this week's talks would almost certainly take place in South Africa.
"We are ready for peace talks on Thursday," he said.
"We are going to prepare for the meeting between our president (Kabila) and Mr Mobutu, what is feasible, the modalities. It will be just a practical session," Kongolo added.

A ceasefire, the departure of Mobutu and the integration of the Zairean government and rebel armies would be the main issues for an eventual meeting between both leaders, he said. The rebels have repeatedly refused a ceasefire before negotiations.

Kongolo said Bizima Karaha, who lead a rebel delegation to an Organisation of African Unity summit in the Togolese capital Lome last week, would lead the rebel team to the talks with Mobutu's representatives.

He said rebel forces were 60 km (37 miles) from Mbuji-Mayi, the diamond capital of Zaire, and would take it or the southeastern city of Lubumbashi, capital of Shaba mineral-rich province, by the end of the week or possibly even by Thursday.
The rebels have seized a quarter of Africa's third largest country since October and are following a strategy of fighting while talking in their bid to oust Mobutu, who has ruled since 1965.
